RE: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Skyler Brooks
Member ID: W379841926
Reference Number: POC-9F671E8F0E-86300
Date of Notice: 2026-08-07
Requested Service/Procedure: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-03

To the Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (Reference Number POC-9F671E8F0E-86300). The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I am submitting the clinical documentation below, which I believe demonstrates that an adequate and well-documented trial of conservative treatment has already occurred, and that additional findings support proceeding to surgery now.

1. Documented conservative treatment already completed
- Symptom duration: 14 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Supervised physical therapy: 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, with 18 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Medication trial: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- Injection therapy: A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-04 provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.

These records show a supervised, multi-modal conservative treatment course (physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and injection therapy) sustained over more than a year, which I ask the plan to review in full as part of this appeal.

2. New and worsening objective findings since conservative care
- MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-10 demonstrates a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. Articular cartilage is preserved, and the Kellgren-Lawrence grade is 1.
- On examination, the patient has positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- Functionally, the patient experiences locking and giving way, and cannot squat or kneel; ambulation is limited to level walking.
- There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. BMI is 29. The patient is a non-smoker.

A displaced, locked bucket-handle meniscal tear is a mechanical problem that conservative therapy (rest, physical therapy, NSAIDs, or injections) cannot resolve, because the torn fragment is physically blocking normal joint motion. The continuation of locking and giving way after 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection indicates that further non-operative treatment is unlikely to change the outcome.

3. Regarding the applicable medical policy
I understand that Wellpoint's musculoskeletal/joint-surgery prior authorization determinations are made using the Carelon Medical Benefits Management "Joint Surgery" Clinical Appropriateness Guideline (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025), which contains a "Knee Arthroscopy and Open Procedures" section addressing CPT 29881. That guideline's General Clinical Guideline section states that a finding of clinical appropriateness depends on the clinician confirming the diagnosis "based on a complete evaluation of the patient," including "a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention." The enclosed records — 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, a 4-month NSAID trial, a corticosteroid injection, a positive physical exam, and a diagnostic MRI — directly document each of these elements, including the patient's response to prior therapeutic intervention.

I was not able to obtain the specific numbered "Clinical Indications" criteria within the "Knee Arthroscopy and Open Procedures" section of that guideline (i.e., the exact duration/type of conservative care the plan requires, or any stated exception for a locked knee with a displaced meniscal tear). I am not quoting or asserting any specific plan language for that section because I have not seen it. I am formally requesting, pursuant to the plan's own guideline provision that "the finding shall include copies of any additional clinical review criteria used in arriving at the decision," that Wellpoint provide the complete text of the specific criteria applied to this denial so that the treating surgeon can respond point-by-point, and that this documentation be sent to both the member and Dr. Okafor.

4. Request for peer-to-peer review
The same guideline section states that if the required elements "are not established with respect to a given request, the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation to understand the individual and unique facts that would justify a finding of clinical appropriateness." Accordingly, I ask that a peer-to-peer conversation be scheduled between the plan's reviewing physician and Dr. Okafor, the treating orthopedic surgeon, to discuss the specific facts of this case, including the locked-knee finding on MRI.

5. Requested action
Based on the above, I request that Wellpoint:
(a) Reverse the denial and approve CPT 29881 for the requested knee arthroscopy/meniscectomy; or
(b) If the denial is not reversed on the record submitted, provide the specific "Knee Arthroscopy and Open Procedures" clinical indications criteria applied to this request, and grant a peer-to-peer review before issuing a final internal appeal decision.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (16 weeks, 18 visits, 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24)
- Medication/treatment records documenting 4 months of NSAID therapy
- Record of corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-04 and documented response
- MRI report dated 2026-07-10
- Office visit/exam notes documenting provocative testing and functional limitations
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, if available]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise of the timeframe for a decision. If this appeal is denied, please include, as required, notice of my right to external review and instructions for initiating it, including contact information for the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Brooks
